title: Static Response of the Strongly Coupled Electron Gas from Diffusion Monte Carlo
authors: Muhammed H. Güneş, Yubo Yang, Vitaly Gorelov, Miguel A. Morales, Matteo Gatti, Lucia Reining, Shiwei Zhang
abstract: The local field factor $G(q)$ of the HEG describes how exchange and correlation modify the response to a static perturbation, and enters dielectric screening, effective electron--electron interactions, and the xc kernel of TDDFT. Accurate zero-temperature data for $G(q)$, however, remain limited to metallic densities, $r_s\leq10$. In this work, we present diffusion Monte Carlo calculations of the static density response function $χ(q)$ and of $G(q)$ for $2\leq r_s\leq100$, and describe and discuss the methodological steps that enabled these calculations. We show how optimization of the perturbing potential in the trial wave function has an important effect, as a poor choice can reverse the sign of the response. A closed-form expression is provided for its optimal value, together with the density dependence of the linear-response window. We further show that backflow correlations leave $χ(q)$ unchanged and that $G(q)$ depends only weakly on system size even at very low density, so that Slater--Jastrow wave functions and modest system sizes suffice. Together, these results provide a practical guide for future QMC calculations of response properties of the electron gas and real materials. Our results agree with previous DMC data at metallic densities for $q>k_F$, and extend them below $k_F$. They also agree with diagrammatic QMC at $r_s=2$. At lower densities, our results show that $G(q)$ develops a nonmonotonic structure at intermediate-$q$, where the response approaches that of the noninteracting gas. Quantitative agreement is seen with finite-temperature path integral Monte Carlo, suggesting that the previously reported finite-temperature structure is inherited from the ground state. Using a parametrization of $G(q)$ that reproduces our data throughout the liquid phase, we relate this structure to short-range order in the pair correlation function and the static structure factor.
summary: This work presents state-of-the-art Diffusion Monte Carlo calculations to determine the static response function and local field factor of the electron gas across a vast density range ($2 \le r_s \le 100$). By refining the methodology, the authors extend reliable calculations significantly beyond previous metallic limits, revealing novel structural features in the response at lower densities.
main_problem: The primary goal is to accurately determine the static response properties, specifically the local field factor G(q), of the strongly coupled electron gas for densities significantly beyond the previously studied metallic regime ($r_s > 10$).
main_result: The authors successfully calculate $\chi(q)$ and $G(q)$ for $2 \le r_s \le 100$, showing that $G(q)$ develops a nonmonotonic structure at intermediate wave vectors at lower densities, which relates to short-range order.
method: The study employs Diffusion Monte Carlo (DMC) calculations on the perturbed energy $E(v_q)$ to extract the static density response function $\chi(q)$ and subsequently $G(q)$ via the Dyson equation.
model_or_system: The system modeled is the Homogeneous Electron Gas (HEG), characterized by the density parameter $r_s$. The calculations are performed using advanced DMC techniques, including optimizing variational parameters and applying finite-size corrections.
key_observables: Static density-density response function $\chi(q)$ and the local field factor $G(q)$.
important_parameters: The density parameter $r_s$ (ranging from 2 to 100) and the wave vector $q$ relative to the Fermi wave vector $k_F$.
main_assumptions:
The methodology relies on the assumption that the linear-response regime can be identified using criteria like Signal-to-Noise Ratio (SNR) and $\chi^2_
u$, and that scaling laws derived from noninteracting systems can guide the calculation across different densities.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the dependence of the perturbed energy $E(v_q)$ on the perturbation amplitude $v_q$ for various densities, showing the optimal variational parameter $\alpha$ dependence on $q/k_F$, and visualizing the finite-size correction $\Delta\chi$ across different system sizes.
paper_structure: The paper details the methodology for calculating $\chi(q)$ and $G(q)$ using DMC, emphasizing the optimization of the perturbing potential and the treatment of finite-size effects. It then presents the results across a wide density range, comparing findings with previous literature and relating the structure to pair correlation functions.
why_interesting: While focused on the HEG, the rigorous application of advanced quantum Monte Carlo methods to calculate response functions provides a benchmark for many-body physics calculations relevant to strongly correlated quantum materials.
